Aero 1.1 makes the local model better at real app work: it knows which apps you have, works in other apps without taking your mouse, keyboard or focus (and says plainly when that isn't possible), reads whole web pages, asks you small questions without stopping the rest of the task, and frees GPU memory while someone views your PC over Remote Desktop.

## Install or update

Aero 1.0 offers this update at startup (**Update now**). New installs:

| System | File | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Windows** 10 / 11 (64-bit) | `Aero-windows.zip` | Extract it, double-click `Update-Aero.bat`, accept the admin prompt. |
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `Aero-macos.zip` | Unzip it, right-click `Install-Aero.command` → Open. |
| **Linux**, any distro | `install.sh` | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/releases/latest/download/install.sh \| sh` |
| Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS | `aero_1.1.0_all.deb` | `sudo apt install ./aero_1.1.0_all.deb` |
| Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Alma, openSUSE | `aero-1.1.0-1.noarch.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./aero-1.1.0-1.noarch.rpm` |
| Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS | `PKGBUILD` | `makepkg -si` |
| Any Linux, by hand | `Aero-linux.tar.gz` | `sh Aero/install.sh` |

Models, chats, memory, settings, keys, tunings, HAPO profiles, MCP servers, skills and mods carry over. New settings start at their defaults.

## What's new

- **Name an app and Aero finds it.** It reads what's installed (Start menu, Installed apps, Store apps, link handlers on Windows; `.desktop` files on Linux; `/Applications` on macOS) and tells the model which program you mean and how to start it. "Open my Bloxstrap" finds Bloxstrap, and knows Roblox links open through it. New tools `app_find` and `app_launch`; a launch counts only when a new process or window of that app really appeared. Settings → Apps lets you search, add your own names and see launches that worked.
- **Background means background.** Every app action now says how it ran: through UI Automation, through window messages, or with your real mouse and keyboard. Values are read back after they're set; clicks are checked against the window before and after; input an app ignores is reported as failed, never as done. Measured on Windows 11, two common routes (UI Automation's SetValue on classic text fields and BM_CLICK on buttons) brought the target window to the front; 1.1 uses routes that don't, and guards every action.
- **Your mouse and keyboard need your OK.** Anything that would use them shows **Foreground control required** first (Allow once, Allow for this task, Deny), waits until you stop typing, holds an exclusive lock so two agents never share them, and puts your window back afterwards. **Strict Background Only** (Settings → Tools) refuses them altogether.
- **One agent per window.** Two agents can't act on the same app window at once; the second is told who has it.
- **Questions that don't stop the task.** When one detail is missing ("Which Gmail account should I check?"), the model asks with a card in the chat and keeps doing everything else. Answer whenever you like, even after the reply finished: the task continues from your answer.
- **Whole pages, with sources.** Aero's browser now runs in the background (no window) unless you or a sign-in need one, gives each agent its own tab, and reads entire pages as sections with headings, links and tables (`browser_read_sections`, `browser_extract`). Results say exactly what was left out. `fetch_url` returns sections too. Strict offline is also enforced inside the browser.
- **Meeting documents from email.** `meeting_doc` turns meeting emails into a Word document for a week in your time zone: invitation updates and cancellations, conflicts, links and prep, nothing invented, never overwriting a file, checked by reopening it. The built-in skill *meetings-from-email* walks the model through it (mail through a connected MCP server or Aero's browser after you sign in yourself).
- **Remote Mode.** While someone is connected to your PC over Windows Remote Desktop, Aero can run part of the model on the CPU so the remote session has GPU memory, and restores your profile after the last viewer has been gone for a while. Measured on an RTX 5080 with a 27B model at the default 80 %: 1.7 GB of VRAM freed, generation 59 → 21 tok/s. RustDesk offers no verified way to see viewers, so it is only used if you allow likely-but-unverified signs. Settings → Model & tuning.
- **Steps and Stop.** A step list shows what the task is doing; Stop in one chat stops only that chat, releases everything it held and lists what finished and what didn't.
- **Better tool choice.** Measured on 25 new requests, the router plus 1.1's capability hints gave the model the tools it needed for 22 (1.0: 14).
- **Built-in skills:** *meetings-from-email*, *roblox-launch*, *code-project-tests*.

Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/CHANGELOG.md).

## Tested

- 218 automated tests pass on Windows 11 (Python 3.12), and the suite runs on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS in CI.
- Live on Windows 11: background typing and button presses verified with the window in front, the cursor and the clipboard unchanged; ignored input reported as failed; stale controls refused; minimized windows handled without restoring them.
- Live in Edge through Playwright: a long page read below the fold with its source, table rows, a form filled and checked, a stale element refused.
- Remote Mode's split measured on an RTX 5080 (planned and measured GPU share both 79.83 %).

**Not tested:** a real Remote Desktop or RustDesk session from another machine (simulated only), real Gmail accounts, a real Roblox launch, macOS and Linux desktops, AMD and Intel GPUs. See [the test matrix](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/docs/V1.1_TEST_MATRIX.md) and [limits](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/docs/V1.1_LIMITATIONS.md).
